My daily data got truncated around late May, but Yahoo shows the top close was 779.09 on October 6, 2026. I want to cross-check that against the full dataset for September through November, including the most recent November 16 reading, to confirm whether the actual daily peak differs from the highest monthly close in September.

Now I'm sketching out the chart design: aligning both series at their peaks (day 0) using trading days, since the current cycle only has 29 trading days of data after the October 6 top compared to the 2000 dot-com crash's much longer aftermath. I'm planning one chart showing the year leading into the peak plus the limited post-peak window for both series, and a second chart showing the full dot-com decline over 650 days with a horizontal marker at today's -5% drawdown level so viewers can see where we currently stand relative to that historical path. I also want to calculate comparative stats like pre-peak run-up gains and drawdown magnitude at the same point after the peak for both eras.

I'll use unadjusted closing prices for consistency between the index and SPY, build everything in one script that also generates the charts, then append a new section to the report and commit it along with a CSV of the aligned daily data.
